subject: Hosted API commit tiers & rate guardrails — Bluehaven initial ask
messages:
From: Taylor Reeves <taylor@bluehaven.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bluehaven Procurement <procurement@bluehaven.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit tiers and rate protections - initial ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the latency and cost profile looked promising. We ran a quick internal projection and think Bluehaven can commit to a hosted API arrangement, but we need strong rate protections baked into the commercial terms before we can finalize a preferred vendor list decision.

Rough picture:
- Target committed usage: 2.0B tokens/month for a 12-month initial term (pilot for Q3 then scale in Q4).
- We expect usage growth and want a per-token anchored discount schedule (breakpoints at 1B / 2B / 4B tokens).

Must-haves from our side:
1) Price lock on per-token rates for the first 12 months (no upward CPI pass-through except for documented exceptions).
2) MFN clause: if Redwood offers a materially better committed pricing to another customer for the same product/commit structure during the term, we want parity.
3) CPI cap or cap on annual price increases — ideally <= 3% annually; open to limited carve-outs.

We attached our projected usage file and an initial list of legal questions. Can you share a strawman counter and confirm whether Redwood is open to MFN + a CPI cap for a 12-month fixed period? Also include your preferred contracting timeline and procurement contacts.

Thanks,
Taylor Reeves
Head of Platform Partnerships, Bluehaven Analytics
Attachments: Bluehaven_ProjectedUsage_Q2Q3.xlsx, Bluehaven_RFP_legal_questions.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Reeves <taylor@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers and rate protections - initial ask

Hi Taylor — great to meet yesterday, and thank you for the clear asks + the usage file. We can absolutely structure a committed tier with breakpoints and a defined price anchor. A few quick points and next steps: 

- Short answer on MFN/CPI: we can accept a limited MFN and an annual CPI cap if we agree the MFN is scoped to materially similar committed products and volumes. Exact % cap on CPI is something we need to align on internally — I’ll push an ask for a 3% cap but need to confirm tradeoffs.
- To move quickly: I’ll circulate an internal counter this morning with pricing ranges and specific carve-outs for MFN (e.g., excludes promotional pilots, marketplace channel listings, or multi-year strategic commitments).
- Please confirm the procurement timeline and the Bluehaven legal contact to receive a redline. Also, would a 12-month fixed price plus an option to extend at pre-agreed tiers be acceptable?

I’ll loop in our pricing and legal leads (cc’d) and share a neat counter by 1pm PT.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API commit tiers and rate protections - internal counter guidance

Team — quick pricing / legal guidance for Bluehaven. I ran the numbers against their projected 2B tokens/mo baseline. Recommendation: 

1) Commercial structure (preferred): 18-month term (committed), tiered per-token discounts:
   - 0-1B tokens: $0.00045/token
   - 1B-3B tokens: $0.00035/token
   - 3B+: $0.00028/token
2) Price lock: 12 months firm on committed per-token rates. After month 12, annual CPI-based adjustment capped at 4.5% unless customer extends/upsizes.
3) MFN: offer a narrowly scoped MFN — parity for materially similar committed-tier deals (same term length, same minimum committed tokens, excluding marketplace promotions and channel-reseller arrangements). Limit duration to the active term + 90 days.
4) Consider offering an OTC credit buffer: if CPI adjustment is applied after 12 months, provide a one-time usage credit equal to 1% of annual committed spend as goodwill for customer budgeting.

Attachments I’m dropping into the thread: internal guidance document (rate_protections_guidance.pdf) and a draft counter (Redwood_Counter_BH_v1.docx). If they insist on an unconditional enterprise-wide MFN or a <=3% CPI cap, we should push for longer term (24 months) or higher commit.

Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Reeves <taylor@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, legal@bluehaven.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal: commit tiers & rate guardrails (draft)

Hi Taylor — thanks for the clear ask and the usage model. Please find our initial commercial counter below (high-level; legal will circulate redlines):

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 18-month committed agreement (auto-renew option).
- Committed baseline: 2.0B tokens/month (monthly true-up at the end of each month).
- Per-token pricing (committed tiers):
  * 0–1B: $0.00045/token
  * 1B–3B: $0.00035/token
  * 3B+: $0.00028/token
- Price lock: committed per-token rates fixed for the first 12 months. After month 12, annual adjustment tied to CPI-U, capped at 4.5% per year.
- MFN: Redwood will grant MFN limited to materially similar committed deals (same product, term, and committed minimums). MFN excludes: marketplace listings, channel/reseller deals, and promotional pilots. MFN survival: active term + 90 days.
- Additional concession: one-time credit equal to 1% of committed annual spend if a CPI increase is applied after month 12.

We prefer to keep MFN scoped to materially similar, not unconditional across all customer segments. If Bluehaven requires broader MFN or a tighter CPI cap (<=3%), we can consider: (a) increasing committed term to 24 months, or (b) raising the committed minimum to 3B tokens/mo to offset risk.

Legal next steps: please share the name and email for your contracting lead and any internal redline timelines. We can generate a draft SOW + commercial exhibit for review. If this looks directionally correct, I’ll send a DocuSign link for the commercial term sheet and loop in our legal counsel.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Counter_BH_v1.docx

From: Taylor Reeves <taylor@bluehaven.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bluehaven Procurement <procurement@bluehaven.ai>, legal@bluehaven.ai, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal: commit tiers & rate guardrails (draft)

Marissa / Soojin — appreciate the quick counter. A few items from our side: 

- The tiered rates look reasonable.
- MFN: Bluehaven cannot accept MFN that excludes channel or marketplace in practice — we need parity across public offers to avoid being undercut by partners. If you cannot grant a broader MFN, we’ll need stronger CPI protection or an escrow/penalty mechanism.
- CPI cap: 4.5% is higher than our target. If you can reduce to <=3% we will sign the 18-month term now. If not, we will request a 24-month term with a 3% cap or an up-front commitment credit to offset potential increases.

Legal note: please send the draft term sheet to legal@bluehaven.ai. Our procurement timeline is tight — procurement needs fully executed commercial terms by May 14 to hit Q3 onboarding. Attached: Bluehaven_RFP_legal_questions.pdf.

Taylor
Head of Platform Partnerships, Bluehaven Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood counterproposal: next steps and negotiation playbook

Team — quick alignment for negotiation handoff: 
1) Prioritize: keep MFN scoped (preferred) and offer two trade-off packages to present to customer:
   A) 18-month term, CPI cap 4.5%, scoped MFN, 1% annual credit on CPI application (low upfront concession).
   B) 24-month term, CPI cap 3.0%, broader MFN (wider parity), modest uplift in per-token price (about +10% across tiers) or one-time committed payment to be paid up-front (customer choice).
2) Prepare draft SOW + commercial exhibit and share DocuSign link for package A first (faster path).
3) Sales to confirm procurement deadline (May 14) and loop legal for redline turnaround (48 hours).

I’ll update HubSpot with the two-package options and estimated margin impact. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345-BH

Rishi
VP, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
